title: OPPE 1 (2025 Jan) Set 1 · P1: Check is even or divisible by 5
description:
Write a function is_even_or_divisible_by_5 that takes an integer as input and returns True if it is even or is divisible by 5, else False.

Examples:
- is_even_or_divisible_by_5(8) -> True (8 is even)
- is_even_or_divisible_by_5(10) -> True (10 is even and divisible by 5)
- is_even_or_divisible_by_5(15) -> True (15 is divisible by 5)
- is_even_or_divisible_by_5(7) -> False (not even nor divisible by 5)

NOTE: This is a function type question, you don't have to take input or print the output, just have to complete the required function definition.

title: OPPE 1 (2025 Jan) Set 1 · P2: Deinterleave Even and Odd Indices in String
description:
Write a function deinterleave that takes a string s as input and returns a new string where the characters at even indices are placed before the characters at odd indices.

Examples:
- "abcdef" -> "acebdf"
- "12345" -> "13524"

NOTE: This is a function type question, you don't have to take input or print the output, just have to complete the required function definition.

title: OPPE 1 (2025 Jan) Set 1 · P3: Make dictionary from elements in index of lists
description:
Write a function make_dict_from_elems_in_index that returns a dictionary consisting of a single key-value pair formed as follows:
- the key is the element at the given index from the list keys
- the value is the element at the given index from the list values

Assume the index is always within valid bounds for both lists.

Example:
>>> keys = ['apple', 'banana', 'cherry']
>>> values = [10, 20, 30, 40]
>>> make_dict_from_elems_in_index(keys, values, 1)
{'banana': 20}
>>> make_dict_from_elems_in_index(keys, values, -1)
{'cherry': 40}

NOTE: This is a function type question, you don't have to take input or print the output, just have to complete the required function definition.
starter_code: def make_dict_from_elems_in_index(keys: list, values: list, index: int) -> dict:
suffix_code:
keys = eval(input())
values = eval(input())
index = int(input())
print(make_dict_from_elems_in_index(keys, values, index))

title: OPPE 1 (2025 Jan) Set 1 · P4: Count unique even and odd numbers
description:
Write a function count_unique_even_odd that takes a list of integers and returns a dictionary with the count of unique even and odd numbers in the list. The dictionary has the keys "even" and "odd".

Example:
>>> l = [1, 2, 2, 3, 4, 5, 5, 6, 9]
>>> count_unique_even_odd(l)
{"even": 3, "odd": 4}

The unique even numbers are 2, 4 and 6 (count 3). The unique odd numbers are 1, 3, 5 and 9 (count 4).

NOTE: This is a function type question, you don't have to take input or print the output, just have to complete the required function definition.

title: OPPE 1 (2025 Jan) Set 1 · P5: Vowel count of words
description:
Write a program that takes a string and counts the number of vowels in every word. The program should then print each word followed by the count of vowels in parentheses.

Assume words are separated by a single space. Vowels can be uppercase or lowercase.

Example:
Input: Computer science is amazing
Output: Computer(3) science(3) is(1) amazing(3)

NOTE: This is an I/O type question, you need to write the whole code for taking input and printing the output.
input_format: A string in the first line.
output_format: A string with the vowel count of each word in parentheses after each word.

title: OPPE 1 (2025 Jan) Set 1 · P6: Student Score Filter
description:
Given the data of student scores in a dictionary where keys are student names and values are lists of scores, write a function filter_students(data, criteria) to filter student names based on the following criteria:
- 'excellent': students with average score >= 85.
- 'good': students with average score between 50 (inclusive) and 85 (exclusive).
- 'all_pass': students with all scores >= 50.
- 'balanced': students whose difference between max score and min score is <= 10.
Any other criteria returns an empty list. The names are returned in the order they appear in the dictionary.

Example: data = {"Alice": [90, 80, 85], "Bob": [40, 50, 60], "Charlie": [30, 40, 20], "Ram": [78, 92, 85, 79, 81], "Babu": [67, 70, 75], "Kumar": [100, 100, 100, 100, 100, 100, 40]}
>>> filter_students(data, 'excellent')
['Alice', 'Kumar']
>>> filter_students(data, 'good')
['Bob', 'Ram', 'Babu']
>>> filter_students(data, 'all_pass')
['Alice', 'Ram', 'Babu']
>>> filter_students(data, 'balanced')
['Alice', 'Babu']

NOTE: This is a function type question, you don't have to take input or print the output, just have to complete the required function definition.
starter_code: def filter_students(data: dict, criteria: str) -> list:
suffix_code:
data = eval(input())
criteria = input()
print(filter_students(data, criteria))

title: OPPE 1 (2025 Jan) Set 1 · P7: W Pattern
description:
Given an integer n (where n > 0), print a pattern with n rows made of a vertical bar (|) on the left and right sides of each row, and a forward slash (/) and a backslash (\) in the middle. The two slashes start together at the top and move diagonally away from each other towards the bottom, forming a "W"-like peak. There should be no spaces to the right of the last bar.

Examples:
n = 1
|/\|

n = 2
| /\ |
|/  \|

n = 3
|  /\  |
| /  \ |
|/    \|

NOTE: This is an I/O type question, you need to write the whole code for taking input and printing the output.
input_format: A single integer n, representing the number of rows in the pattern.
output_format: The pattern with n rows, as described.
